data.name: Rollin
data.gender_notes: Rollin is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Old English ‘rullan’ meaning ‘to roll’. Rollin was a common name in the Middle Ages, particularly among the nobility. It signified power, strength, and was also associated with the idea of progress or movement forward. The name Rollin carries the meaning “Powerful, Strength” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Rollin usually hope their child will grow to embody powerful, strength and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the journey of faith and the strength to carry on during life's challenges.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rollin total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Rollin was popular among the Anglo-Saxon and Frisian peoples, and its association with nobility and power was reinforced through literary works such as Chaucer's "Canterbury Tales," in which one of the pilgrims is named Sir Rollin. Rollin was also a common name among early settlers in America, perpetuating its association with strength, power, and the journey forward.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian tradition, the name Rollin holds spiritual significance as a reminder of the roll or cycle of life, the idea that life is not static but continually moving and evolving. Rollin is also a reminder of the rolling away of the stone from the tomb of Jesus, signifying new beginnings and the forgiveness of sins. In the spiritual sense, Rollin serves as a reminder of the importance of continuing the journey of faith, rolling forward in the journey towards God.
